static_answer:
**Problem Summary**

A 52-year-old man with chronic diarrhoea, neuropathy, weight loss, and new heart failure has imaging most consistent with an infiltrative cardiomyopathy, likely amyloidosis, but the aetiology and subtype remain unconfirmed.

**Interpretation**

The echocardiographic and CMR pattern (symmetric LV thickening, relative apical sparing on strain, elevated native T1, ECV approximately 50%, diffuse subendocardial LGE) strongly supports an infiltrative process, most characteristically amyloidosis. The negative monoclonal workup makes AL amyloidosis less probable but does not exclude it. PYP planar grade-1 uptake with a heart-to-contralateral-lung ratio above 1.42 is equivocal; the non-biopsy algorithm for ATTR requires grade-2 or higher uptake, so this result does not establish ATTR. The mildly reduced alpha-galactosidase A with negative GLA sequencing and unmeasured lyso-Gb3 leaves Fabry disease unexcluded, though the subendocardial LGE distribution and markedly elevated ECV are atypical for Fabry.

**Needed before final aetiology**

Tissue confirmation with Congo red staining and amyloid typing (mass spectrometry or immunohistochemistry) is required to establish the diagnosis and subtype. If amyloid is confirmed, TTR genetic testing or further imaging clarification distinguishes ATTRwt from ATTRv. Lyso-Gb3 measurement should close the Fabry gap. The initial haemodynamic values are historical; current status is unknown.

fixed_records.text: At the initial examination, blood pressure was 80/46 mmHg and heart rate 52 beats/min.
Initial NT-proBNP was 887 pg/mL, high-sensitivity troponin T 23.9 ng/L, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL and eGFR 62.7 mL/min/1.73 m².
No updated vital signs are supplied for the later investigation-review point.
Echocardiography showed symmetric left-ventricular wall thickening, septal thickness 14.1 mm, LVEF 36%, grade-II diastolic dysfunction and relative apical sparing on strain.

Cardiac MRI showed diffuse wall thickening, high native myocardial T1, extracellular volume 49.85%–52.47%, and diffuse subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement involving the left ventricle and interatrial septum.
Serum/urine immunofixation and serum free-light-chain testing found no monoclonal gammopathy.
Alpha-galactosidase A activity was 1.70 µmol/L/h (laboratory reference >2.0); GLA sequencing found no pathogenic variant. Plasma lyso-Gb3 was not measured.
Technetium-PYP scintigraphy showed planar grade-1 myocardial uptake and a heart-to-contralateral-lung ratio >1.42; acquisition timing and additional technical details are not supplied here.
